Jozabad son of Jeshua (Ezra 8:33) and Jozabad among the Levites in Ezra 10:23 are both Levites of Ezra's time, but nothing ties them together.
Neh 10:10 and 10:12 list Shebaniah twice in one list of Levites; a list does not repeat a man, so two men of that name.
Sherebiah of Mahli (Ezra 8:18) and Sherebiah in Neh 10:12 are plausibly the same Levite a decade or so apart, but the text never says so.

Bani the people's leader (Neh 10:14) and the 'Bani' tied to Ezra 10:38 (where the Berean text reads 'descendants of Binnui', so that record rests on a variant) may be one clan head or only the same family name; Bani and Binnui interchange as clan names elsewhere (Ezra 2:10, Neh 7:15), so the text leaves it open.

Jabal and Jubal are named as brothers, sons of Lamech (Gen 4:20-21); the names are alike but the sons are two.
The lists of David's sons born in Jerusalem run in the same order, Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon (2Sam 5:14, 1Chr 14:4), and Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon (1Chr 3:5).
note: A reading, not the text's statement. FOR: the parallel lists give the same four sons in the same order, 'Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon' (2Sam 5:14; 1Chr 14:4) against 'Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon' (1Chr 3:5), with only the first name differing, and 1Chr 3:5 introduces them with the same words, 'born to him in Jerusalem'. AGAINST: the two spellings are not identical in Hebrew, and 2Sam 5:14 does not say they were Bathsheba's, as 1Chr 3:5 does.

why: Shammah is Jesse's third son (1Sam 17:13); Shimeah is David's brother, father of Jonadab (2Sam 13:3) and of Jonathan (1Chr 20:7, where he is called Shimei).
note: A reading, not the text's statement. FOR: Shammah is the third of Jesse's sons (1Sam 17:13) and the parallel list gives Shimea as third (1Chr 2:13); Shimeah is David's brother (2Sam 13:3), and his son Jonathan is called son of David's brother Shimei in 1Chr 20:7, so one brother's name is spelled Shammah, Shimea, Shimeah and Shimei. AGAINST: no verse says outright that Shimeah is the third son; the spellings differ in Hebrew, and David's brothers could include half-brothers.

why: Dan was Rachel's maid's son (Gen 30:6), Dinah was Leah's daughter (Gen 30:21); different children of Jacob.

note: A reading, not the text's statement. FOR: both lists of Jesse's sons run Eliab first, Abinadab second, and the third is Shammah (1Sam 17:13) or Shimea (1Chr 2:13), the same position under the same father. AGAINST: the Hebrew spellings differ, and the lists are not stated to be one list.

note: A reading, not the text's statement. FOR: Joktan's sons are listed in the same order in the two parallel genealogies, 'Obal, Abimael, Sheba' (Gen 10:28) and the same three at 1Chr 1:22, with only one vowel differing (Obal/Ebal in the Hebrew). AGAINST: the Hebrew names are spelled differently, and the Chronicler's list is not marked as a copy of Genesis.
